items.title: How Weaker U.S. Industrial Output Data May Test Caterpillar's (CAT) Backlog Resilience
items.summary: In recent days, Caterpillar was hit by weaker-than-expected U.S. industrial production data for July, which pointed to cooling activity and raised questions about demand for industrial goods across the sector. This softer macro signal matters for Caterpillar because it contrasts with prior optimism around its record backlog and broad end-market demand, sharpening the focus on how resilient that order book really is if industrial activity slows. items.title: Review & Preview: Chips Crumble
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.2%, hurt in part by companies like Caterpillar and Goldman Sachs, which have exposure to the faltering AI trade.  Better-than-expected results despite a slow housing market helped Home Depot’s stock head higher on Tuesday, and energy stocks continued to climb on the back of higher oil prices.  “Monday’s weakness spilled into the new day, and the reasons are familiar,” notes Joe Mazzola, Head Trading & Derivatives Strategist at Charles Schwab.

items.title: FTAI Aviation, EMCOR, Caterpillar, Wabash, and MYR Group Shares Are Falling, What You Need To Know
items.summary: A number of stocks fell in the morning session after the latest industrial production report showed slower-than-expected growth for July. Data from the Federal Reserve indicated that U.S. industrial production rose by 0.2%, which was half of the 0.4% increase that analysts polled by The Wall Street Journal had anticipated.
